claims.text: The target HEA contains multiple transition metals in near-equimolar ratios.
The target HEA crystallizes as a homogeneous, single-phase bcc lattice.
High mixing entropy enforces formation of a homogeneous, stable bcc structure.
A homogeneous, stable bcc structure promotes conventional electron–phonon coupling.
Conventional electron–phonon coupling enables low-temperature s-wave Cooper pairing in the target HEA.
Homogeneous atomic distribution minimizes local compositional fluctuations and disorder.
High mixing entropy produces a uniform lattice environment with spatially consistent electron–phonon interactions.
A uniform lattice environment enhances conventional s-wave pairing and leads to robust superconductivity.
Reducing mixing entropy while retaining a similar bcc structure will produce greater local compositional variation.
Greater local compositional variation in the control will weaken electron–phonon interactions.
The lower-entropy control may consequently have a lower critical temperature or a broader superconducting transition.
The target HEA will exhibit a superconducting transition around 7–10 K.
The target HEA will have a sharper resistive superconducting transition than the lower-entropy control.
The target HEA will show a clearer diamagnetic response than the lower-entropy control.
The target HEA will have a higher upper critical field than the lower-entropy control.
Ambient-pressure measurements avoid extrinsic disorder and ensure that any transition is intrinsic and related to electron–phonon coupling.
The proposed mechanism applies to HEAs that retain a stable bcc phase under ambient conditions.
Significant phase inhomogeneity or extreme extrinsic disorder may prevent the predicted superconducting behavior.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state identifies the target homogeneous bcc HEA as the initial state, whereas the baseline calls the reduced-entropy control alloy the starting state.
